key_insight: A fine-tuned multimodal LLM could extract autism-related behavioral features from short home videos with clinician-level agreement and strong diagnostic performance.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a scalable way to support earlier autism assessment by turning everyday videos into structured behavioral scores for downstream clinical use.
method: Fine-tuned Gemini 2.5 Pro with low-rank adaptation on 400 clinician-rated home videos.
Trained the model to predict 30 previously validated behavioral features.
Tested performance on 99 held-out children and compared outputs with clinician ratings and diagnosis pipelines.
evidence_signal: On 99 held-out children, feature-level agreement improved by 40% overall, 27 of 28 evaluable features got better, and direct ASD diagnosis F1 rose by 53%, with classifier pipelines reaching 77% accuracy and 86% AUC.
watch_item: Results come from a relatively small held-out sample and require external validation before real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: Fine-tuning a multimodal large language model for clinician-grade autism behavioral scoring from short home videos
